title: Inducing Artificial Uncertainty in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.13595v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In safety-critical applications, language models should be able to characterize their uncertainty with meaningful probabilities. Many uncertainty quantification approaches require supervised data; however, finding suitable unseen challenging data is increasingly difficult for large language models trained on vast amounts of scraped data. If the model is consistently (and correctly) confident in its predictions, the uncertainty quantification method may consistently overestimate confidence on new and unfamiliar data. Finding data which exhibits enough uncertainty to train supervised uncertainty quantification methods for high-performance models may therefore be challenging, and will increase in difficulty as LLMs saturate datasets. translated_title: 在语言模型中诱导人工不确定性
translated_abstract: 在安全关键应用中，语言模型应当能够用有意义的概率来表征其不确定性。许多不确定性量化方法需要监督数据；然而，对于在海量抓取数据上训练的大型语言模型而言，寻找合适的未见过的、具有挑战性的数据变得越来越困难。如果模型对其预测始终（且正确地）保持自信，那么不确定性量化方法可能会在新颖和陌生的数据上一贯地高估置信度。因此，找到展现出足够不确定性的数据来为高性能模型训练监督式不确定性量化方法可能颇具挑战，并且随着大语言模型使数据集趋于饱和，这一难度还将不断增加。为了解决这一问题，我们首先引入了在语言模型中诱导人工不确定性的问题，然后研究了在缺乏……的情况下，如何在极其简单的数据上诱导人工不确定性的方法。
tldr: 该论文提出在语言模型中诱导人工不确定性的新问题及方法，以解决当数据集饱和、难以找到足够不确定的监督数据时，不确定性量化方法可能失效的挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the problem of inducing artificial uncertainty in language models, proposing methods to address the challenge that supervised uncertainty quantification may fail when sufficiently uncertain training data becomes scarce as LLMs saturate datasets.
